articles.title_orig: Hospitals Rush to Patch Java Vulnerabilities
articles.title_zh: Hospitals Rush to Patch Java Vulnerabilities
articles.content_orig:
On November 17, 2026, details emerged exposing a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in OpenJDK, tracked as CVE-2026-114938 (dubbed "Java4Shell") with a CVSSv4.0 score of 9.2. The bug exists in the optimized assembly code handling AVX-512 Base64 decoding, allowing remote unauthenticated attackers to cause heap memory corruption. Triggering this flaw on affected systems can lead to remote code execution.
The "Java4Shell" vulnerability and exploit were discovered and disclosed by security firm Calif.
CVE-2026-114938 is a memory-corruption vulnerability residing in the optimized Base64 decoding intrinsic engine of the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). To maximize performance, OpenJDK uses an optimized implementation on supported x86-64 processors, based on AVX-512 VBMI instructions. However, the optimized assembly code miscalculates the output array bounds when handling inputs that contain an unexpected number of trailing padding characters (=).
When an input containing a specific sequence -such as 64 A characters followed by a single = - is parsed, the decoder's length calculation underflows to a negative value. This calculation mismatch causes an out-of-bounds write past the allocated heap memory buffer. Attackers can leverage this to overwrite adjacent object metadata, which can lead to code execution. We have proved that remote exploitation is feasible against standard Java applications such Jenkins, Confluence, and Apache Tomcat.
Like other memory safety issues, exploitation is possible with AI, but is not trivial. Our AI based vulnerability research harness, Wiz Atlas , managed to find and build a proof-of-concept exploit for this vulnerability within 2 hours, even before the full details were disclosed. Having said that, generalizing the exploit for an arbitrary target is difficult. We should expect adversaries to target commonplace Java applications, where specific builds and memory layouts repeat across targets. Motivated adversaries may tailor exploits with AI for specific targets, including home-grown applications.
Web Application Firewalls can help mitigate some of the exploits as they emerge in the wild. Since this vulnerability is rooted in OpenJDK itself, many possible code paths using user inputs may lead into the vulnerable code path, so it’s unlikely that WAF rules will be able to cover all possible paths, and will never be able to cover home grown applications completely. The best solution is upgrading to the latest OpenJDK version.
Prioritize externally facing, packaged Java applications, and make sure they are either patched or restricted from public access. Upgrade home-grown Java applications and update to the latest OpenJDK version containing the fix.
The vulnerability affects OpenJDK versions 17.0.6 and later, as well as downstream distributions, provided they run on x86-64 hardware supporting AVX-512 VBMI instruction sets (ARM64 processors are unaffected). Affected software distributions and hardware include:
OpenJDK Distributions: Amazon Corretto, Eclipse Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Azul Zulu, BellSoft Liberica, SAP SapMachine, Red Hat OpenJDK, and Oracle Java SE (specifically versions 8u511b33-perf, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 27.0.1.0.3).
Vulnerable CPU Architectures: Intel Xeon (Ice Lake, Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids, Granite Rapids) and AMD EPYC/Ryzen (Zen 4 or newer).
Proven Vulnerable Applications (Pre-Auth RCE): Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, Keycloak, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins, and custom frameworks built on Spring Boot, Apache Struts, Apache Kafka Broker, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, Netflix Spinnaker and Apache Tomcat.
Security teams should immediately prioritize the following mitigation steps:
Audit and Patch: Identify all systems running OpenJDK 17.0.6 or later on AVX-512-capable x86-64 hardware. Apply the official security patches released on November 17, 2026, or update to downstream vendor-supplied builds immediately.
Verify Hardware Vulnerability: Run the following command on Linux systems to check if your infrastructure is physically affected:
If all four CPU flags are present in the output, the host runs the vulnerable hardware execution path.
Implement JVM Runtime Workarounds: If immediate patching is not possible, apply one of the following flags to JVM startup parameters to completely neutralize the vulnerability. They may have performance impact on the application.
Disable Base64 Intrinsics (Recommended): -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics
Disable AVX-512 execution (x86-64 only): -XX:UseAVX=2
Isolate Internet-Facing Services: Temporarily restrict external network access to vulnerable management portals (e.g., Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak) until mitigations or updates are deployed.
Wiz customers can use the pre-built query and advisory in the Wiz Threat Center to search for vulnerable instances in their environment.
On November 17, 2026 at 20:35 UTC, versions 1.26.1 & 1.26.2 of the Microsoft PyPI package agent-framework were published with an added credential stealer.  The package gets almost 200k downloads a month. The malicious versions have since been quarantined.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic IPO: AI lab considers increasing the offering as investor demand surges
articles.title_zh: Anthropic IPO: AI lab considers increasing the offering as investor demand surges
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic is considering upsizing its initial public offering, people familiar with the details told CNBC, as the artificial intelligence lab weighs setting the price well above $80.
The company closed its order books and locked in total demand on Tuesday, setting the stage for the Claude creator's eagerly awaited Nasdaq listing. Institutional demand for the offering is around $400 billion, while retail demand is approaching $100 billion, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly.
The orders are indications of interest and are not binding. All of the details are subject to change, and Anthropic will make final decisions Wednesday afternoon, the people said. Anthropic is expected to set its final IPO price after market close Wednesday.
Demand for the offering is higher than it was for Elon Musk's SpaceX , even though the rocket maker had a bigger market offering. SpaceX debuted on the Nasdaq in June in by far the biggest IPO on record, ultimately raising $85.7 billion.
The AI lab said last week that it would offer 825 million shares in the IPO at a price range of between $70 and $78 per share, which would net up to $64.35 billion at the high end of that range.
A representative for Anthropic declined to comment.
Anthropic's listing is a major test for the AI industry, which has experienced a set of recent shocks, including a dramatic backlash that was felt at the polls in the midterm elections and last week's ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . The market was already jittery on concerns that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for many data center developers and neoclouds.
Tech's biggest companies have significant exposure to Anthropic, as an investor, partner or customer. Amazon and Google both own stakes valued at over $100 billion, and a group of tech companies, including Google, Microsoft , Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices agreed to collectively invest $26 billion in the IPO. Anthropic, meanwhile, is a buyer of costly systems from Nvidia, Google, Amazon and AMD.
"I think if we do this right, we can create an age of miracles where humanity is able to solve problems that have eluded us for millennia," Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in Anthropic's roadshow video . "We have to make sure that all the risks, all the ways that things can go wrong with this technology, we very carefully address those risks as we bring the benefits and as we have a viable business at the same time."
Amodei co-founded Anthropic alongside a handful of other researchers less than six years ago, after the group collectively defected from OpenAI. The company is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude , and it primarily sells its products and services to other businesses.
Anthropic has been racing to maintain an edge over OpenAI and Google in the enterprise market, and it experienced a period of explosive growth in 2026, driven largely by the popularity of its AI coding tool, Claude Code. OpenAI has confidentially filed for an IPO and has said a debut is likely in 2027.
For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said, it generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year, according to its prospectus. The company reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said.
Anthropic said in an amended filing that its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the previous month.
The company has faced plenty of challenges during its meteoric rise over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, leading to two high-profile disputes with the U.S. government this year. Its prospectus included more than 90 pages of risk factors for investors to consider ahead of its IPO.
"Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the company's prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort."

articles.title_orig: Here’s how much Medicare Part B premiums are rising in 2027
articles.title_zh: Here’s how much Medicare Part B premiums are rising in 2027
articles.content_orig:
Medicare Part B premiums will rise by 3.2% in 2027, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services announced Tuesday .
The standard premium will rise by $6.50 per month to $209.40, totaling a $78-per-year increase.
The 2027 increase, far smaller than the nearly 10% increase enrollees faced in 2026, is in line with the 3.25% increase projected by Medicare's trustees.
According to the CMS, "The increase in the 2027 Part B standard premium and deductible is mainly due to projected increases in healthcare spending."
Here's what you need to know before the increases are applied in January.
The Medicare Part A deductible, which beneficiaries pay if they are admitted to the hospital, will rise by $40 to $1,776 in 2027.
The Medicare Part A premium will be $597 per month, a $32 increase from $565 in 2026.
According to the CMS , it is paid by:
Anyone aged 65 and older with fewer than 40 quarters of coverage, plus certain people with disabilities.
Uninsured people aged 65 and older with fewer than 30 quarters, and certain people with disabilities who have exhausted other entitlements.
Those with at least 30 quarters (or a spouse with 30 or more quarters) will pay a reduced rate of $328.
Roughly 9% of people with Part B pay an income-related surcharge on top of their monthly premium.
The annual deductible for all Medicare Part B beneficiaries will increase by $9 to $292 in 2027.
In 2027, individuals with modified adjusted gross income above $112,000, or couples filing jointly above $224,000, will pay more. At the top tier, individuals with an income of $500,000 or more and couples earning $750,000 or more will pay $711.80 a month.
Married people who live with their spouse but file separate tax returns pay the standard $209.40 Part B premium if their income is $112,000 or less. Above that, they pay a total of $670 a month, rising to $711.80 for those earning $388,000 or more.
A small group of kidney transplant patients can keep Part B coverage of immunosuppressive drugs for a standard premium of $125.70 a month.
Those with higher incomes who pay Part D premiums face separate income-related surcharges between $15.40 and $96.40 a month on top of their plan's premium. The surcharge is paid to Medicare and is either deducted from Social Security checks or paid directly.
People who have their Part B premium deducted from their Social Security checks will keep less of the cost-of-living adjustment next year.
For the average retiree, the $6.50 Part B increase will eat into the $75 monthly COLA boost, leaving them with about $68.50 more a month.
Most beneficiaries will have the standard $209.40 Part B premium withheld from their checks. Higher earners will pay more, with total monthly Part B premiums reaching as much as $711.80 and Part D surcharges up to $96.40.

articles.title_orig: Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard lore
articles.title_zh: Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard lore
articles.content_orig:
Designers’ notes: The Doom of Lord Carrard lore
The latest Arcane Journal, The Doom of Lord Carrard , will be available to pre-order this weekend. To find out more, we undertook our own quest into the depths of the Warhammer studio to speak to the designers about the lore of the latest supplement.
JTY: Since the release of Warhammer: The Old World, we’ve been following the events of Settra the Imperishable’s war against the Old World. We’ve seen his armies advance through the Border Princes and navigate the peaks and valleys of the Vaults en route to the borders of Bretonnia. We’ve even seen what happens when an ancient Liche Priest leads an army of the Undead into the depths of Athel Loren . But what we haven’t covered in much detail is what caused all this turmoil in the first place.
In Arcane Journal – the Doom of Lord Carrard we decided to address this. We wanted to explore the charnel realm of Nehekhara in greater detail, and we felt Lord Carrard’s quest allowed us to do just that.
Much of the narrative is told from the perspective of the Bretonnians, giving us a relatable lens through which to view the horrors of the Land of the Dead. This allowed us to introduce Lord Carrard himself, a baron from the realm of Brionne, and establish his relationship with Sir Lothar of Kasos Rock, once a noble knight of Carrard’s court but now an outcast dwelling in the Border Princes .
It is the arrival of a messenger from Sir Lothar that sets in motion the events that are to follow. Bringing the grim forebodings from Sir Lothar’s court, the messenger warns of a great evil stirring in the Land of the Dead and implores Lord Carrard for his aid in vanquishing it. Rather than muster armies on the strength of vague portents, the baron elects to undertake a quest, riding in the company of his closest companions to the court of his former friend.
The next part of the story is told through the recollections of Sir Varo, one of the few to return and bring word of Lord Carrard’s fate, and of the evil that has been awakened in the Land of the Dead. Through Varo we learn of the Bretonnians’ journey to the accursed city of Zandri, from where we explore Nehekhara itself, coming face to face with the horrors of the Land of the Dead as the bold knights cross the deserts and battle the undead horrors placed before them. Accompanied by a wealth of stunning new art, this tale casts a whole new light upon this accursed realm, giving the reader a sense of the scale of the civilisation that once ruled the deserts of the Great Land, and the horrors a traveller might encounter in deserts haunted by looming horrors beneath skies shrouded behind impregnable dust storms.
But that’s not all. Arcane Journal – The Doom of Lord Carrard also examines ancient Nehekhara, in particular the major cities of that once-vibrant land, and the royal dynasties that once ruled over them. Delving into such ancient history was a fun challenge, and reading about the cities and dynasties of the Land of the Dead will hopefully inspire readers. There are lots of ideas here for theming your own collections of Tomb Kings of Khemri to reflect the armies of a particular city or monarch.
It’s always fun to explore the World of Legend, and shining a light on the events that led to Settra's climactic invasion was especially enjoyable. This was a story we were keen to tell, and we can’t wait to see how it will inspire readers!
Thanks, JTY! The new Arcane Journal is available for pre-order from Saturday, along with a wealth of reinforcements for the Tomb Kings of Khemri in the form of Skeleton Warriors , Skeleton Archers, Horsemen and Horse Archers , and Skeleton Chariots. Join us later in the week when we’ll be learning more about the rules in the Arcane Journal.

articles.title_orig: Key House Republican pours cold water on $50 billion FAA funding ask
articles.title_zh: Key House Republican pours cold water on $50 billion FAA funding ask
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON — The Trump administration’s request for $50.1 billion in new Federal Aviation Administration funding after a nationwide ground stop strangled air travel is running into skepticism from both parties on Capitol Hill.
The funding request was suddenly increased from $30 billion after the hourslong ground stop Friday caused delays and cancellations for passengers across thousands of flights.
The formal funding ask was conveyed in a Tuesday letter signed by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who refused to apologize or accept responsibility for the failure, blaming it on predecessors and Congress. The letter, cosigned by FAA chief Bryan Bedford and White House budget director Russell Vought, stated the money was needed “to deliver a truly world-class air traffic control network.”
After publicly reproaching Congress for the failure last week, Duffy met privately with Senate Republicans on Tuesday to make his case on Capitol Hill.
The closed-door briefing was contentious. The transportation secretary was “yelled at” by multiple Republican senators during his briefing, according to a person in the room who was not authorized to speak publicly about the private discussion.
When it was over, Senate Republican leaders and Duffy notably held their news conferences separately.
Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., stopped short of endorsing the full funding figure, saying only that the GOP is unified around the belief that “safe skies is an incredibly important priority.”
“We will see what the traffic will bear, what’s achievable,” he said, calling it a “discussion to be had” on the dollar amount.
Duffy met with only Republicans on Tuesday, not Democrats — even though the regular government funding process requires bipartisan support.
And Democrats were left wanting a better explanation, particularly as Duffy has pointed fingers at them. And members in both parties noted that President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” included $12.5 billion for air traffic control that still has not been fully used up.
“Look, we have not been given the answers. They have not come clean,” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., told reporters on Tuesday. “At his first press conference, all Duffy did was attack Democrats, and he asked for $50 billion when they haven’t even spent the $12 billion we’ve given to them. I have little faith in them.”
Facing Republican questions on the matter, Duffy insisted that the $12.5 billion was insufficient for the specific upgrades he deemed necessary in this situation.
Other Democrats are vexed by the FAA funding request.
“I generally support the idea of investing in air traffic control, but $50 billion sounds like an awfully round number,” said Sen. Brian Schatz, D-Hawaii, who’s poised to become majority whip and also sits on the Senate Appropriations Committee.
The issue is wrapped up in a larger debate about funding the government ahead of a Dec. 11 deadline to avoid another shutdown . Congress could either reach a deal by then on new funding, punt it to next year with a stopgap bill, or fail to act and allow a shutdown.
Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, said air traffic control is “absolutely not a partisan issue” and that Congress will work to make sure that any funding is “paid for in a responsible way.”
Republicans are also considering a party-line “reconciliation” bill to approve military funding without the need for Democratic votes; Democrats are likely to resist additional military funds unless the Iran war comes to an end. Other provisions could be added to such a bill — if it materializes before Republicans lose control of Congress. Thune indicated Tuesday that it is still an open question, as Republicans would need to pass a budget resolution by Thanksgiving to pull it off. It would be a long, arduous process requiring near-total GOP unity in both chambers, and it would need to begin soon in order to finish this year.
Duffy said he’s agnostic on how the funds get passed when asked by NBC News why he only met with Republicans on Tuesday.
“I have met with Democrats. I’ve spent hours on the phone with Democrats. Get along with them well. They understand this issue,” Duffy said Tuesday, speaking to reporters separately after meeting with GOP senators. “I’m not going to tell them how to do their work, but I’m telling everybody what we need. I’m making a nice ask, and I’m going to let them work their process.”
One of the Democrats whom Duffy spoke to was House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., the likely next House speaker.
“I appreciated the conversation,” Jeffries told reporters. “There are still more questions than answers in terms of what happened, why it happened, how do we prevent it from happening again.”
Jeffries added that he wants a briefing on the FAA ground stop and other recent outages, saying: “These developments are troubling, and it’s unclear if it’s all infrastructure-related or whether there’s some malignant activity.”
When asked about Duffy’s $50.1 billion request, outgoing House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., said Republicans would work with the administration to fund “as much of that as we can.” He pointed to the $12.5 billion already approved for FAA modernization and did not specify a timeline or whether Congress would pursue a supplemental funding package.
I am a field producer for NBC News based in Washington, D.C., covering all things politics.
Sahil Kapur is a senior national political reporter for NBC News.
Julie Tsirkin is a correspondent covering Capitol Hill and the White House.

The commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, is asked which governments will take part in the loan, given that at least four – Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovakia – have signalled they do not want to be involved.
She strikes a determined tone as she says it’s different from the previous loan (where three countries were given an opt-out) and all countries need to participate as she directly links it with the EU’s budget.
“So shared budget, shared responsibilities. There’s a very important point,” she says.
She says that since the loan has two elements – civilian and military – those countries that do not want to provide any funding for Ukraine’s military can still take part in the other part of the loan.
“I’m very confident that we will agree by 27 because, as I said, all 27 member states support Ukraine explicitly.”
Well, let’s see about that.
That ends the press conference – I will bring you any reaction from the four potential breakaway leaders when we get it.
And, on that note, we will be closing the blog for today .
The EU executive has proposed a €45bn (£37.5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues ( 11:10 , 11:11 , 11:16 , 11:23 ).
Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria have said they do not intend to take part in the latest funding round for Ukraine, and their leaders are yet to comment on today’s announcement ( 15:40 ).
Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said the new EU financial support for Ukraine would “greatly help Ukraine, our resilience and our diplomacy,” amid continuing talks with US and other allies ( 13:41 ).
The Coalition of the Willing is set to meet in Berlin on Thursday for further talks on helping Ukraine , including a first meeting of the new Europe negotiating team with Donald Trump’s US peace envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner .

Back to Ukraine , our global affairs correspondent Andrew Roth reports from Kyiv on growing pressure on the capital’s mayor Vitali Klitschko as the city continues to be hit by Russian attacks and energy outages.
“ It may seem unfair to blame a wartime mayor facing daily strikes from Russian ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones for the devastating energy crisis now hitting major Ukrainian cities. Among the worst hit is Kyiv where many homes only have power for four hours a day now, well before the winter months when freezing temperatures will put far more strain on the remaining infrastructure.
But critics argue that the city’s management failed to prepare for the dire power shortages despite clear signs the Kremlin would target Kyiv with strikes that would seek to end its viability as a livable city.”

Elsewhere, a Spanish court is investigating the singer Julio Iglesias over complaints that he sexually abused and physically assaulted two female employees who worked at his properties in the Caribbean.
The announcement of the investigation by the Audiencia Nacional comes almost 11 months after Spanish prosecutors shelved the women’s complaints , arguing the country’s courts had no jurisdiction as the alleged offences took place outside Spain.
But the human rights NGO Women’s Link Worldwide , which is representing the women, has successfully argued that the Audiencia Nacional has jurisdiction over the case and Iglesias’s Spanish nationality provides sufficient grounds to try the case in Spain. It filed a new criminal complaint on the women’s behalf on 3 September.
The allegations emerged in January this year after a three-year joint investigation by the Spanish news site elDiario.es and the Spanish-language TV network Univision Noticias, which gathered testimony from 15 former employees who worked for the now 83-year-old singer between the late 1990s and 2023.
The two complainants – a domestic worker and a physical therapist who were employed at Iglesias’s mansions in the Dominican Republic and the Bahamas – allege the veteran entertainer subjected them “to inappropriate touching, insults and humiliation … in an atmosphere of control and constant harassment”. The offences are alleged to have occurred in 2021.
In a statement released on Wednesday, the Audiencia Nacional said it was investigating the women’s complaint, which accuses Iglesias of “offences against sexual freedom, as well as offences involving bodily harm and degrading treatment”.
Iglesias , who has sold more than 300m records during his six-decade career, has denied all the allegations and said he would defend himself against what he described as “a serious affront”.
Earlier this week, we covered the ongoing government formation talks in Sweden, where – 66 days on from the 13 September election – there is still no new administration in place.
And it looks as if the Swedish electorate is losing patience with the nominal election winners, the Social Democrats, led by former prime minister Magdalena Andersson.
A new Novus poll showed the centre-right Moderates unexpectedly coming out on top in the latest polling , overtaking the Social Democrats as the largest party for the first time in a decade, SVT reported.
The party of the still-incumbent prime minister, Ulf Kristersson , has the support of 26.5% of voters, ahead of Andersson’s Social Democrats on 24.9%.
The Tidö grouping of centre-right to far-right parties polls 6.3 percentage points ahead of the centre-left bloc that narrowly won September’s vote.
The latest numbers will increase pressure on the four centre-left parties to agree on a coalition government and retake the initiative – currently held by Kristersson – ahead of the Christmas deadline set by the parliament speaker, Andreas Norlén ( Europe Live, Tuesday ).
But the left-leaning parties are struggling to agree on a way forward, with two of the four parties locked in contradicting demands on the composition of the new government.
The new parliament has already failed twice to agree on a new PM ( Europe Live, 15 October and 3 November ), with a third attempt expected before the end of the month. If a fourth attempt fails too, the country will go back to the polls in the new year.

Announcing the plan to lend Kyiv the money in 2027, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen , said: “ We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table . And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.”

The four central and eastern countries are net beneficiaries of the EU budget, while Germany is the largest payer and Ukraine’s biggest EU donor.
The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said he hoped for the swift adoption of the loan and was counting on the support of all EU member states: “Strong support for Ukraine is the best signal to Russia that this war must end,” he wrote on X.
Zelenskyy convinced EU leaders last month that his country faced a €70bn funding gap in 2027 . The EU pledged to cover €45bn and wants Ukraine’s other allies to cover the rest.

articles.title_orig: Palestinians flee refugee camp as Israel begins operation in central Gaza
articles.title_zh: Palestinians flee refugee camp as Israel begins operation in central Gaza
articles.content_orig:
Israeli forces killed three Palestinians during a new operation in central Gaza on Wednesday, according to hospital officials, in the first broad ground offensive since a “ceasefire” was signed more than a year ago.
Al Jazeera correspondents on the ground reported that Israeli tanks were operating near Salah al-Din Street, east of the Nuseirat refugee camp and north of the Bureij camp.
An Israeli air strike targeted the town of al-Mughraqa, north of Nuseirat, killing one person and wounding several others, an official at al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera.
Reporting from Gaza City, Al Jazeera’s Hind Khoudary said many Palestinians were fleeing areas in central Gaza as the Israeli operation got under way.
“We have been seeing people in eastern parts of Maghazi and Bureij, and people who are close to Salah al-Din starting to evacuate and flee the area due to the fact that there were huge explosions heard, live ammunition, and artillery shelling in that area,” Khoudary said.
“The Israeli forces in their announcement did not issue an evacuation order for people who are living in this area. They just mentioned that there is a military operation that is going to start, they are going to destroy the infrastructure and they are going to start demolishing in this area,” she added.
Earlier on Wednesday, the Israeli army said the operation aimed to “eliminate a threat” to its forces operating in the area of the “Yellow Line”, which demarcates the Israeli-occupied area of Gaza, and was established under the “ceasefire” agreement signed between Israel and Hamas in October 2025.
In a statement, the Israeli military said: “We reserve the freedom to act and manoeuvre whenever necessary to eliminate any immediate threat in the Gaza Strip.”
Hamas condemned the Israeli operation as a “flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement”.
“Forced evacuation orders and the displacement of citizens carried out under the threat of violence and bombardment constitute a war crime and a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law,” the group said in a statement.
“The occupation’s actions are aimed at herding citizens into a narrow strip of the Gaza Strip, further exacerbating the ongoing humanitarian catastrophe,” it added.
Hamas said it holds Israel and the United States responsible for “the repercussions of the military operation and the crimes committed against civilians”.
Before the announcement of the Israeli operation, two Israeli drone attacks on Gaza killed at least two people, hospital officials told Al Jazeera.
Al-Shifa Hospital reported that one person was killed and others were wounded in an attack on the Sheikh Ijlin neighbourhood in southwestern Gaza City.
In a separate attack, Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital reported that one person was killed in Deir el-Balah in central Gaza, where the hospital had earlier reported an injury.
Earlier on Wednesday, Gaza’s Ministry of Health said that hospitals had recorded seven deaths and received 15 wounded people in the previous 24 hours.
Six people were killed by Israel over that period while one died from injuries caused by an earlier attack, the ministry said.

articles.title_orig: Costco sees surge in panic buying after string of tech outages, report says
articles.title_zh: Costco sees surge in panic buying after string of tech outages, report says
articles.content_orig:
Consumers are panic-buying at Costco, snapping up generators and other emergency-preparedness items in response to a recent string of technology outages , according to investment firm Mizuho Securities.
"Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights, and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales at Costco," Mizuho analyst David Bellinger wrote in a report.
Shoppers are "pantry-loading," while 21 of the retailer's 26 "high-ticket generators" were sold out online as of Sunday night, he added.
The recent outages, which blocked access to Microsoft apps , snarled flights nationwide and hindered banking activities at various times during the past week, are raising questions among Americans about a larger cybersecurity threat, CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman said on "CBS Mornings" on Wednesday.
The companies affected by the outages have said they were due to issues such as routine maintenance or upgrades, while the Federal Aviation Administration blamed its nationwide ground stop last week on a contractor updating its flight system.
"All of them have denied that cyberattacks are to blame," Gutman said. "Still, the system failures are fueling online speculation about a larger cyber threat."
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that there's "zero evidence" that the recent outages in the U.S. are linked.
"The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA . The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Rubio said during a news conference in the Philippines.
Costco didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
The close timing of the outages highlights the country's increasing reliance on technology, John D'Arcy, a Temple University professor who researches cybersecurity and information technology failures, told CBS News Philadelphia.
"Our systems are so much more complex and so much more interconnected than they ever have been in the past, that when we just have one failure, the effects are much more dramatic," D'Arcy said.
The surge in panic buying could lift Costco's sales, Bellinger wrote. He raised his target price for the company's stock to $1,150 from $1,100. Other big-box stores, including Walmart and Sam's Club, could see similar "pantry-loading lifts," he added.

articles.title_orig: Another short-seller announces a bet against Nvidia over possible ties to China
articles.title_zh: Another short-seller announces a bet against Nvidia over possible ties to China
articles.content_orig:
House Democrats have demanded Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s son turn over years of Nvidia trading records, internal communications, and encrypted messages as they investigate whether the Trump administration’s China chip policy benefited the Lutnick family’s financial interests.
Reps. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), Gregory Meeks (D-NY) and Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-Calif.) sent a five-page letter Tuesday to Brandon Lutnick , chairman of Cantor Fitzgerald, seeking records tied to the investment firm’s Nvidia-related holdings and business dealings in Southeast Asia.
The lawmakers are probing whether Howard Lutnick used his position to block restrictions on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing company suspected of smuggling billions of dollars worth of restricted Nvidia AI chips to China.
“Did the Secretary of Commerce seriously and perhaps irreversibly compromise US national security interests to make money for his adult children and Cantor Fitzgerald?” the lawmakers asked the younger Lutnick.
Howard Lutnick, who led Cantor Fitzgerald as chairman and CEO from 1996 until his confirmation in February 2025, transferred his ownership interests in the firm to trusts benefiting his adult children, Brandon and Kyle.
At the time of Lutnick’s confirmation, Cantor held more than 3.5 million Nvidia shares valued at over $1.3 billion, according to reports cited by the Democrats. The firm reduced its holdings by roughly 49% between September 2025 and March 2026, but still holds hundreds of millions of dollars in Nvidia stock.
The Democrats allege Lutnick’s resistance to adding Megaspeed to the Commerce Department’s Entity List of companies banned from buying AI chips helped keep Nvidia’s stock price elevated while Cantor reduced its holdings.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has reportedly identified Lutnick as the primary obstacle to blacklisting Megaspeed, despite intelligence concerns that its CEO, Alice Huang, was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to compromise Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang through a romantic relationship.
Recently uncovered photos show Alice Huang cozying up to the Nvidia boss at dinners , drinks and technology events across Asia.
A former Commerce official told The Post last week that Lutnick refused to publish a proposed export-licensing rule in July 2025 despite other agencies approving the document.
The Democrats’ letter also raises questions about Cantor’s financial ties to Southeast Asian data centers that use Nvidia chips to serve Chinese customers, potentially circumventing US export restrictions.
The lawmakers want records of every Cantor trade involving Nvidia securities since January 2024, including transaction dates, quantities and the names of those responsible. They also want records of any actual or contemplated Nvidia investments held by President Trump and Howard Lutnick, as well as communications between Cantor and Commerce officials.
Notably, the Democrats want to know Cantor’s policies on encrypted and disappearing messages, as well as whether anyone involved in Nvidia trades or data center projects communicated with Commerce officials through Signal, WhatsApp or Telegram.
The Democrats also want records of Cantor’s business dealings in China and Southeast Asia dating back to January 2020, including investments, financing activities and regulatory approvals from Chinese government agencies.
Brandon Lutnick has until 5 p.m. Dec. 1 to produce the initial documents, with Raskin, Meeks and Kamlager-Dov also demanding the immediate preservation of emails, texts, encrypted messages and records stored on personal devices.
The Commerce and Justice departments said in a statement released Tuesday that the Megaspeed investigation began in 2024, with investigators requesting Nvidia sales records in May 2025 and interviewing Alice Huang the following month. The Justice Department later took the lead in the criminal investigation, reportedly after Nvidia’s general counsel contacted the Commerce Department seeking an update on the Megaspeed probe.
“We are confident that a full review of the facts will demonstrate that we have operated our business ethically and in full compliance with all applicable rules and regulations,” a Cantor Fitzgerald spokesperson said in a statement to CNBC.
Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.
The spokesperson also disputed claims that Cantor held a substantial proprietary position in Nvidia, saying its holdings primarily came from equity swaps executed for clients and shares purchased to hedge those trades. The reduction in those holdings reflected clients unwinding their positions, not Cantor independently deciding to sell, the rep claimed.
The firm also described its Southeast Asian data center ties as ordinary investment banking business, calling allegations that they influenced government decisions “baseless.”

articles.title_zh: Israeli tanks roll into central Gaza in first ground operation since ceasefire began
articles.content_orig:
Israeli tanks advanced in an area of ​the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, witnesses said, and the Israeli military said its forces were targeting Hamas infrastructure outside areas that Israel controls in ⁠the enclave.
Witnesses said some Israeli tanks rolled onto the main Salahudeen road, west of the Yellow Line that marks the boundary of the two-thirds of the Gaza Strip still under Israeli control despite ⁠a ceasefire that has ​lasted more ⁠than a year.
An Israeli airstrike near the army raid killed one person, Palestinian medics said.
The medics ⁠said separate Israeli airstrikes had killed two other people ​earlier ⁠in the day in ‌ Deir al-Balah and Gaza City.
An Israeli military spokesperson told NBC News that the military was carrying out an operation targeting “Hamas infrastructure” west of ‌the Yellow Line in central Gaza ‌and that it had struck a militant in southern Gaza earlier on Wednesday.
The lates confirmed that it was the first ground operation since the U.S. brokered ceasefire came into effect in October 2025 .
The truce halted major fighting in the Israel-Gaza war although it has not stopped Israeli attacks or secured Hamas’ disarmament.
The spokesperson had no immediate comment on other strikes.
Israel, which says Hamas has recently been regrouping and rearming, has stepped up attacks against the Islamist group. Hamas has accused Israel of attempting to derail the U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement.
Gaza health ‌authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been ​killed since the ceasefire went into effect, while ‌the Israeli military says five Israeli soldiers have been killed.
Palestinian authorities say more ⁠than 74,000 people in Gaza have been killed in the military campaign ‌that Israel ​launched there after Hamas-led fighters killed ‌about 1,200 people in southern ​Israel in an attack on October 7, 2023.

articles.title_zh: Grand Theft Auto VI Xbox achievements revealed
articles.content_orig:
With GTA 6 set to release on November 19, 2026, many fans have been wondering how long it will take to complete all of the trophies and achievements in the game in order to get the platinum or mythic achievements. Well, GTA 6’s story is going to be long, and its achievements are even more of a grind to get.
Obviously, it’s always somewhat difficult to predict exactly how long it will take to complete Grand Theft Auto 6 , as people have different skill levels; however, from what we’ve been able to gather from people who have actual knowledge of the game’s length, you’re looking at around 50 hours to complete the campaign with nearly 100 missions in total across five individual chapters ( first revealed in 2025 ).
Each mission will, of course, vary in length and take different players longer or shorter depending on their individual skills, but 50 hours seems to be the consensus average.
Rob Nelson, head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar Games , was interviewed by The New York Times, and here’s an interesting excerpt:
“I hope that there will be people that want to get up, have a cup of coffee, shower, get dressed, go out for a little exercise,” Nelson said. His 80-hour play-through of the game in February included the main story and some optional goals with narrative ramifications . Routines can escalate quickly. “Interact with some people, explore, maybe get into some trouble,” he added. “Rob some places, make some money.”

If you’re familiar with Red Dead Redemption 2, it’s probably a similar length and has been “officially” logged at 196 hours total to complete on average.

articles.title_orig: Hims & Hers launches new peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy
articles.title_zh: Hims & Hers launches new peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy
articles.content_orig:
Hims & Hers Health on Wednesday said it will offer five formulations of peptides and longevity treatments compounded in the U.S. as part of the initial rollout of its Peptides+ platform, all of which are not approved by regulators.
Even as it announced the new products, Hims & Hers acknowledged it has more to learn about how best to use the peptides and how effective they are — underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the growing space.
The new offerings come after the federal government eased restrictions on compounding certain unapproved peptides, which are short chains of amino ​acids. Those products have exploded in popularity among fitness and longevity enthusiasts who attest that they help with muscle growth, rapid injury recovery and anti-aging, even though most lack evidence from robust human trials.
Hims in late October launched an early access list for the upcoming peptide offerings, and more than 10,000 people signed up within 15 days, a company spokesperson said in a statement.
None of the company's specific compounded products are approved by the Food and Drug Administration. But Hims said they are authorized by law and formulated by pharmacies "that adhere to rigorous quality standards and are licensed and inspected by state boards of pharmacy."
The products include compounded formulations of sermorelin, a peptide that stimulates growth-hormone release and is marketed for recovery, body composition and anti-aging; glutathione, a peptide promoted ‌for anti-aging and athletic recovery; and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, or NAD+, a coenzyme that plays a role in cellular metabolism.
The company will also offer compounded versions of vitamin B-12, a vitamin needed to make red blood cells, build DNA, and maintain healthy nerve function, and L-carnitine, an amino acid derivative that helps the body turn fat into energy. The FDA has approved certain prescription forms of both peptides for established medical uses, primarily for diagnosed deficiencies in those compounds.
Hims said it plans to add more peptides and therapies made in the U.S. over time. That includes BPC-157, an unapproved peptide derived from a protein found in human gastric juice that is marketed for healing processes. The company also aims to introduce another unapproved peptide called TB-500, which is derived from a naturally occurring protein in the body and is marketed for broader, systemic soft-tissue recovery and flexibility. Most of the research on both has been conducted in animals, not humans.
To receive the products, members on the Hims platform will start with an assessment of health history and goals with a licensed provider trained in peptide therapies, who can tailor a personalized plan to their needs, if appropriate.
The company said it intends to use its communication platform to check in with patients and ensure they are seeing desired results.
"If they're not, we need to do something about it," Dr. Anant Vinjamoori, Hims chief medical officer, told CNBC. "We need to, you know, adjust the dose when that's appropriate, or in some cases consider other compounds that's maybe a better fit. And of course, there will also be cases when we need to refer people to other care options."
However, Vinjamoori said there's still uncertainty over how to best use the peptides.
"We don't have all of this data that we're used to having with compounds like this," he said. "We have the opportunity to get it right, and I think we see that as our responsibility with a company of our size, our skill, and resources to really lead."
Vinjamoori added that people who have serious illnesses, such as cardiovascular disease, liver disease and kidney disease, will not be candidates for the compounds for now.
Meanwhile, Andrew Huberman, a well known neuroscientist, podcaster and Stanford University School of Medicine professor who recently joined Hims' board of directors, in a statement called compounds "real medical treatments, not just a wellness trend." He said Hims provides safe access through "trusted sourcing and physician oversight."
But health experts raised concerns about the broader mainstream marketing of peptides in the U.S. and accessing them on telehealth platforms.
"With peptides, I think you have to view them the same way you would view any drug that hasn't been rigorously tested," said Joshua Kritzer, a chemistry professor at Tufts University. "Without actual testing, all you have is anecdotal information, and that's just not enough information to put a substance in your body."
Kritzer said the lack of large clinical trials means researchers can't rule out potentially serious, rare complications from peptides — the kinds of risks that have led regulators to reject or pull otherwise effective drugs from the market after they underwent comprehensive testing in humans.
Without that testing, it's also unclear how telehealth firms, physicians and pharmacies can make decisions about what doses patients should take, said Paul Knoepfler, a cell biology and human anatomy professor at UC Davis Health. While some people rely on anecdotal data from real peptide users, "the dosing for these products really has not been established," he added.
Knoepfler said one risk is that injecting too much of a synthetic peptide into patients could trigger "weird immune responses that are really bad for one's health" because the body might recognize it as foreign.
"With the peptides, it's very loosey-goosey," Knoepfler told CNBC. "How does one even know what would be the effective amount for whatever you're hoping it will do, and what amount would have more risks?"
But he said the more contact patients can have with physicians around taking a compounded peptide, the better. Providers, including those tied to telehealth firms, should make sure patients are well-informed about the possible risks and unknowns of a given product and consider their preexisting conditions, cancer history and other medications, Knoepfler said.
That appears to be consistent with the approach Hims & Hers is taking. The company says patients who use the peptide and longevity products can also use its Care+ offering, which pairs treatment with ongoing support. That includes twice-a-year lab testing to track their progress and the ability to message providers trained in peptide therapy around the clock with any questions.
Still, Kritzer argued that having a doctor who only knows a patient from online, essentially mail-order platforms or websites "is not enough supervision to put you on a prescription medication," especially an unapproved one.
Hims' ability to legally sell some of these peptides stems from a major shift in federal oversight by the Health and Human Services Department. It issued a policy in October that says the Food and Drug Administration will not take enforcement action against licensed pharmacies, federal facilities or physicians that compound and dispense six unapproved peptides while formal rules are reviewed.
In practice, that means these pharmacies and other firms can now offer them, even though the peptides aren't yet on the FDA's official list of ingredients compounding pharmacies are allowed to make. It does not translate to formal approval of the specific peptides.
The policy followed a 2023 decision by the Biden administration where the FDA restricted compounding pharmacies from producing popular peptide formulations due to safety, impurity and immune-reaction concerns.
HHS Secretary ​Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has supported broader access to peptides, calling himself a "big fan" of the treatments and arguing that restrictions were driving Americans to potentially unsafe products from overseas. Kennedy has previously described using BPC-157 to treat a muscle injury.
The announcement also comes after Hims in February 2025 acquired a California-based peptide manufacturing facility equipped with advanced peptide synthesizers.
The evidence for peptide efficacy varies by compound.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia’s RTX Spark Desktops Imagine They Can Actually Compete With the Mac Studio
articles.title_zh: Nvidia’s RTX Spark Desktops Imagine They Can Actually Compete With the Mac Studio
articles.content_orig:
New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC.
With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work.
Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops.
Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC.
As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks.
RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system.
Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks.
RTX Spark desktops are equipped with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128GB of unified memory, delivering up to 1 petaflop of AI performance. Ten-gigabit Ethernet connectivity enables fast transfers of large datasets, model files and creative assets between RTX Spark compact desktops and networked storage.
This advanced hardware unlocks incredible capabilities for creators, developers and AI enthusiasts, including:
New compact desktops are available for purchase from ASUS, Dell and MSI, joining the RTX Spark family of laptops available today. Mini PCs from Acer, GIGABYTE and HP are coming soon, along with the Microsoft Surface RTX Spark Dev Box .
Native CUDA support and Linux development tools through Windows Subsystem for Linux give developers a foundation for building and running local AI workflows. Developers can set up agents with Hermes Agent or NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and fine-tune supported models using Unsloth.
RTX Spark can run creative agents that connect familiar applications and local AI tools, helping creators move from an idea to finished work with natural-language instructions.
NVIDIA Switchyard, now available in Hermes, automatically routes agent tasks between local and cloud models. Everyday tasks can run on device, while advanced reasoning draws on cloud models, helping manage cloud costs across creative workflows.
These capabilities come together in creative workflows that connect Photoshop and ComfyUI through Hermes Agent. Using natural-language instructions, creators can turn sketches into rendered images and animations, or animate an image entirely on device — from isolating a subject and defining its motion to generating the finished video.
NVIDIA brought these workflows to life at Adobe MAX, where attendees used natural-language instructions to turn sketches into rendered images and animations for a shared digital Miami landscape.
The RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR features, already available in ComfyUI, extend the pipeline: a generated clip can be expanded to 60 frames per second and converted to high dynamic range for color grading, all within a single ComfyUI workflow on RTX Spark.
NVIDIA and Adobe are expanding native Windows on Arm support and RTX acceleration across Adobe’s creative applications, helping video editors, photographers, designers and 3D artists work more efficiently on RTX Spark.
Adobe Premiere accelerates a range of AI-powered editing features through NVIDIA TensorRT-RTX , including Enhance Speech, Object Mask, Scene Edit Detection and Auto Reframe — so editors spend less time waiting and more time cutting.
GPU acceleration also extends to Film Impact transition and effects plug-ins. The update improves support for professional video formats, including Canon RAW, Red RAW, ARRI RAW, ARRICORE, ARRI HDE, H.264 and HEVC in MXF, ProRes RAW and long-GOP video. This lets editors realize more than 50% quicker turnaround on everyday H.264 video deliverables.
Adobe Photoshop adds TensorRT-RTX acceleration for the Remove Tool and ArmRTX Spark-native Camera Raw support, helping photographers remove unwanted objects faster and work with RAW images without relying on emulation. At Adobe MAX, Adobe previewed a next-generation image processing engine with extensive GPU acceleration, including interactive Gaussian blur and Light Leaks filters.
Adobe Substance 3D Painter 12.2 is now optimized for RTX Spark with native support on Arm for the first time in public beta. Artists in games, visual effects and visualization can run Substance Painter natively on RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops, with no compatibility layer required.
Adobe Illustrator and InDesign now offer native Windows on Arm versions optimized for RTX Spark. Adobe Illustrator delivers up to 30% higher performance than its emulated version, helping accelerate illustration, graphic design and page-layout workflows on RTX Spark.
Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction into the Cycles viewport, helping artists evaluate lighting and materials with near-final-quality ray-traced previews as they work.
The practical difference is immediate: instead of navigating a noisy, resolving preview, Ray Reconstruction delivers near-final-quality lighting, reflections and materials in the interactive viewport in real time.
DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support requires Blender 5.3 and the latest NVIDIA Game Ready Driver or NVIDIA Studio Driver. Download the NVIDIA App to get automatic notifications when the latest drivers are available, optimize games and applications from a unified GPU control center, and discover the latest NVIDIA tools and software.
Announced at Microsoft Ignite, Windows Server is evolving for organizations that need to run AI closer to their enterprise applications and data.
Microsoft is expanding hardware choice through support for the latest AI silicon, helping customers take advantage of accelerated inference and increasingly capable models in their own environments. NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows platform powered by the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip is expanding to include support for Windows Server 2028.
New accelerator platforms and the breadth of the Windows silicon ecosystem provide customers options at different capability levels and price points for advanced AI development, local inference, and agent workloads at scale.
Also announced at Microsoft Ignite, developers can now bring any GGUF model from Hugging Face and run it within Windows ML using the llama.cpp backend.
The DxCGC backend, now available as an experimental release, is an integration for game developers that compiles and runs machine learning models through DirectX 12, allowing them to execute AI workloads alongside graphics.
Windows APIs let applications integrate platform-provided AI capabilities adding GPU support for AION Instruct and VSR.
Developers can also build high-performance AI models for Windows ML using the command line interface.

🎉 Ricursive Intelligence introduced its first open model: Ripple-65B Preview. The full-stack AI lab builds self-improving systems by co-optimizing hardware, software and models. Ripple-65B Preview was trained on NVIDIA B300 GPUs, refined using NVIDIA Nemotron post-training d

articles.title_orig: The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires
articles.title_zh: The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires
articles.content_orig:
In the space of just five years, Anthropic has gone from unknown start-up to tech giant, worth more than a trillion dollars.
The company behind the AI platform Claude was formed by seven people who left rival OpenAI in 2021 and, in a matter of hours, will become multi-billionaires - on paper at least.
Anthropic is floating the business on the US stock exchange and will sell its shares at between $70 - $78 each.
If they go for the highest price, the founders' shareholdings will be worth at least $18.5bn each.
So, who are these people, all in their thirties and forties, who are about to become incredibly wealthy?
In 2020, Dario Amodei was working for OpenAI, the firm that brought generative artificial intelligence to a mainstream audience, when it launched Chat-GPT.
He decided he wanted to do things his own way, and left, taking his sister Daniela, and five colleagues with him.
Amodei grew up in San Francisco, impressing school friends not just with his academic prowess but also his speed on the running track , and his preoccupation with philosophical and technological questions including the potential of machines to gain consciousness and human longevity.
Initially he studied physics at Princeton and Stanford. But following his father's death from hepatitis C, he switched to biology and biomedical sciences.
Amodei did stints at the Chinese tech giant Baidu and Google before joining OpenAI.
But he began to worry that some people within the company were putting profit before safety, prompting the decision to jump ship.
Now 43, he is Anthropic's chief executive, and the person who, in his sister's words, makes the company "ambitious".
Dario and Daniela Amodei, were close growing up and later shared a flat together in San Francisco with other friends. She followed him into OpenAI and joined him when he left to found Anthropic.
She and her brother have always genuinely liked each other, she says, but the only thing she ever did first, was when he followed her in becoming vegetarian.
Amodei studied English Literature at the University of California Santa Cruz, going on to work for Democrat representative Matt Cartwright.
She has also worked at financial services platform Stripe, where she was head of risk operations.
The 39-year-old is president of Anthropic, manages the executive team, and leads the firm's research, engineering, product, governance and commercial work.
Tom Brown, now 39, followed the Amodei siblings when they left to found their new venture.
He led GPT-3 engineering at OpenAI, and prior to that was at Google on its DeepMind project.
Brown established his entrepreneurial credentials co-founding an app called "Grouper" that helps set up drinks between groups of friends.
He has supported US President Donald Trump's stance on datacentres, arguing that they are "an enormous source of prosperity".
Now as chief compute officer at Anthropic he is responsible for how the company secures and uses its computing resources.
Jack Clark, is another arts graduate among the original start-up's founding members and the only one who is not from North America.
Originally from Brighton in the UK, he studied English Literature and Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia and became a technology journalist, writing for publications including ZDNet UK, The Register, and Bloomberg.
He was caught up in the excitement of artificial intelligence and joined OpenAI, where he worked initially in communications, later becoming its policy director.
Now, 37, Clark is head of public benefit at Anthropic. He also leads the Anthropic Institute, an AI think tank.
Jared Kaplan, 42, is chief science officer at Anthropic, and heads its technical research. He is also an associate professor at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore.
He holds a PhD in physics from Harvard University.
His work on scaling laws - which describe mathematical patterns that show that bigger AI models trained on more data tend to be more consistent - has helped provide AI firms with a framework for predicting AI behaviour, according to Anthropic.
Chris Olah is described as "interpretability research lead" primarily focused on how AI models work with each other.
But according to the New York Times, Olah has spent much of the last year convening meetings with faith leaders from across the religious spectrum.
Described by the newspaper as "boyish" but with "the zeal of an evangelist" the 34-year-old is reportedly exploring the relationship between morality and AI.
He previously led interoperability research at OpenAI, and prior to that was a research scientist at Google Brain.
The Canadian left the University of Toronto early, but later secured a Thiel Fellowship of $100,000, which is a scholarship to help gifted people move into research without a degree.
Sam McCandlish, 36, takes less of a public-facing role than the other founders, but like them will own around 1.6% of the company after its shares go on sale. As a result he too will see his stake crystallise into a hugely valuable asset.
McCandlish is Anthropic's chief architect, and helps shape and implement the company's policy designed to mitigate the risks of AI. Prior to this he worked on safety at OpenAI.
He has a physics PhD from Stanford, and maths and physics degree from Brandeis University outside Boston.

articles.title_orig: Bank outage: How to protect your money when your bank goes offline
articles.title_zh: Bank outage: How to protect your money when your bank goes offline
articles.content_orig:
Customers at JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, U.S. Bank and other major financial institutions reported service outages on Monday, according to Downdetector.com .
Other banks that saw a spike in customer complaints about difficulty accessing their accounts included Capital One, Truist and Wells Fargo, while users also reported problems with the digital payments app Zelle, according to the outage tracker.
However, Downdetector showed that service was back to normal at the banks and Zelle early Tuesday.
CBS News has reached out for comment to Chase, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank and Capital One.
Bank of America told CBS News in a statement that its "systems were operating normally throughout the day yesterday."
Chase Bank's services were experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said Monday.
"Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds," a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. "We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible."
Chase also said in a social media post that a software bug in its systems affected other institutions "when we were party to a transaction involving other banks." The issue is not systemic, the bank added.
Some Chase customers received a message that said, "Some services aren't available. We're working on them. Please try back later."
Bank customers started reporting problems accessing online services on Monday morning. By the afternoon, reports of outages had surged, according to Downdetector.com. As of 2 p.m. ET, nearly 4,800 users had reported problems with Chase, the most of any bank.
Chase customers reported issues accessing their online accounts, including viewing balances and performing transactions such as bank transfers and wire transfers, according to Downdetector.
Bank of America clients reported problems with ATMs as well as online and mobile banking services, according to the outage tracker. A Bank of America spokesperson told CBS News its "systems have been operating normally today."
U.S. Bank customers reported issues with their online accounts and the bank's mobile app. They also had problems transferring funds, while Wells Fargo customers reported difficulty signing in to their accounts, as well as with getting account balances and conducting transactions.
A Chase Bank customer in Texas told CBS News he tried to deposit a check at a Dallas branch early Monday, but the transaction could not be completed. A bank teller told the customer in front of him that the "system was down" without providing additional details, he added, expressing frustration at the lack of clarity about the situation.
A spokesperson for U.S. Bank said its systems were not directly impacted by the cyber outage. "However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays," the company said in a statement to CBS News.
A Capital One spokesperson said it hasn't been affected by the outage and continues to operate normally.
Zelle told CBS News its service was "operating as it should," but that some users could be experiencing issues related to problems at their financial institutions, which could be delaying Zelle payments.
"Consumers use Zelle through participating banks and credit unions, which manage their accounts and hold their funds," a Zelle spokesperson said. "Consumers do not have a separate Zelle account, and Zelle does not hold consumer funds."
Zelle's network operator, Early Warning Services, is owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo.
The banking outages occurred after Microsoft restored services on Saturday following a global outage affecting its Outlook and Teams services, which disrupted users, companies and government operations worldwide. Microsoft said a technical issue caused the outage and that it was not linked to a cyberattack.
The glitches also came only days after overloaded routers forced the Federal Aviation Administration to order a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday, stranding travelers and causing thousands of canceled flights. The FAA said Sunday that airline schedules across the U.S. were returning to normal . (On Monday evening, United Airlines also said it resolved a " widespread system outage " it had been dealing with that afternoon.)
Cybersecurity experts said the root causes of the bank service disruptions, Microsoft outage and FAA system failure, while different on their face, also point to a common problem.
"Our country has seen three very serious technology incidents over the past week," Mike Chapple, an IT, analytics and operations expert at the University of Notre Dame, said in a statement to CBS News. "When we dig into the details, each one has an explanation that makes sense on its own, but they all point to a common theme: the complexity and fragility of the systems that we depend on every day."
He noted that in each case, a technical issue quickly rippled through interconnected systems, causing massive disruptions nationwide.
"We don't yet know much about today's banking system outage, but it appears to stem from a technical issue at Chase that affected other banks through their shared payment networks," Chapple added.
When big companies like JPMorgan Chase experience technical disruptions, their impact often reverberates industrywide, added Karen Panetta, dean of graduate engineering at Tufts University.
"The larger companies have global reach that affords their customers flexibility and seamless integration with other businesses," she told CBS News. "Unfortunately, when one of these backbone providers has disruptions, the downstream effects are magnified. The multiple entities that rely on those services are also affected."
Kayne McGladrey, a security expert and senior member of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, said bank customers might have better luck going to their local branch in person, noting that financial services often still work on site when online banking resources go down.
"Try ATMs, cards, phone banking and branches, which often keep working when the app doesn't," he said in a statement to CBS News.
He also advised people to keep records of any attempted or failed transactions.
"Screenshot failed transactions and error messages, since you may need them for reconciliation or fee waivers. Once service is back, ask the bank to reverse any fees the outage caused," McGladrey said.
He also urged consumers to ignore unsolicited emails about the bank outages, which she warned might be phishing scams. Instead, people should rely on their bank's official communication channels for information, McGladrey said.
Craig Timm, senior director of anti-money laundering at ACAMS, an anti-financial-crime organization, told CBS News he expects criminals to exploit consumer anxiety about potentially losing access to their money, and that consumers should "assume they will be targeted." That's in part because AI lets scammers act fast and at scale.
Timm said common tactics to be alert to include criminals exerting pressure on targets "to take urgent action to protect their funds or restore account access."
"These scams may take the form of fake bank alerts, phishing texts or emails, or social media posts that claim to offer help," he said. "Some schemes aim to steal banking login credentials, while others use malicious links to gain access to a victim's computer."
Edited by Alain  Sherter and Aimee  Picchi
The Associated  Press contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: NVIDIA GPU Drivers Reportedly Writing Up To 30GB Per Hour To SSDs, Echoing AMD’s Recent Driver Bug
articles.title_zh: NVIDIA GPU Drivers Reportedly Writing Up To 30GB Per Hour To SSDs, Echoing AMD’s Recent Driver Bug
articles.content_orig:
Reports are mounting that NVIDIA's GeForce drivers continue writing large volumes of data to the system drive even when the PC is idle. Measurements by affected users show cases reaching 30GB per hour, prompting concerns that the writes could shorten SSD lifespan. The issue comes just after AMD addressed a similar problem, leaving both GPU vendors grappling with storage-load issues in quick succession.
The suspected core of the problem is "NVDisplay.Container.exe," a background process tied to the NVIDIA Display Container LS service. According to an investigation published by TroubleGrid, the process repeatedly overwrites a binary-format log file located at "C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\nvlog.nvlgstg," and the rewriting of the same file—rather than append-style logging—is believed to generate the heavy write volume. Reported symptoms include constant disk access, a surge in host writes, and temporary system stutters attributable to NVDisplay.Container.exe.
A detailed report posted on NVIDIA's official forums confirmed a clear regression in driver 621.14, released on November 4. About 515MB of per-process writes were measured over five minutes from an idle state, compared with less than 2MB under identical conditions on driver 621.01. There are also reports of more than 3GB over 10 minutes and a measurement showing roughly 30GB per hour on the newer 621.24.
These figures, however, are individual user measurements, and it should be noted that Windows' per-process I/O counters do not necessarily match physical NAND write volume. Similar file rewriting was reported in Dell's community in January 2025, with more than 10MB per operation. Complaints about NVIDIA's logging mechanism date back to 2021.
In a newsroom verification as well, the problem reproduced on a Windows 11 system equipped with an RTX 4090, with the gameplay capture feature "Highlights" disabled and the PC left idle. Windows Resource Monitor showed NVDisplay.Container.exe continuously writing about 1.43MB per second to the system drive—equivalent to roughly 5.2GB per hour if sustained. Access to the same nvlog.nvlgstg log file was repeatedly observed. While this measurement is a snapshot and does not establish long-term write speeds or actual NAND wear, it suggests that turning off capture-related features alone may not stop the background logging.
Note: All figures are individual measurements by users or news organizations and may not match physical NAND write volume.
Discussion continues in the community. Some report that writes stopped after disabling NVIDIA's Highlights and ShadowPlay-related features, while others confirm symptoms persist even with the overlay fully turned off. Some users on the latest drivers detect no abnormal writes, suggesting the issue does not occur in every environment.
Reported workarounds include stopping NVIDIA Display Container LS, deleting the log file, and restarting the service, or rolling back to driver 621.01. Permanently disabling the service, however, would prevent NVIDIA Control Panel and NVIDIA App from functioning properly.
NVIDIA has not officially acknowledged the logging issue, and it is not listed as a known issue in the release notes for 621.24, released on November 12. AMD, by contrast, recently acknowledged a similar SSD write issue and introduced a fix in Adrenalin 26.11.1.
The matter bears directly on PC durability and maintenance costs, in that GPU drivers can place continuous, invisible load on storage. In corporate environments running large numbers of machines, increased write volumes could shorten SSD replacement cycles. Users can check whether NVDisplay.Container.exe is continuously writing to the log file using Windows Resource Monitor (press Win+R, type "resmon," and select the Disk tab). Until NVIDIA offers an official position and a permanent fix, users will need to weigh measured data before deciding how to respond.
